claim: Let \(K\) be Kühnel's nine-vertex triangulation of \(\mathbb{CP}^{2}\). For every nonempty proper vertex set \(S\subsetneq V(K)\), the induced subcomplex \(K[S]\) is a simplex when \(S\) is a face of \(K\), and when \(S\) is not a face, \(K[S]\) simplicially collapses to the tetrahedral sphere \(\partial\Delta^{3}\). Hence every proper induced subcomplex is either contractible or simple-homotopy equivalent to \(S^{2}\), with the dichotomy decided exactly by face membership.
integrity: The combinatorial model is reconstructed from published facet-orbit data. Every claimed collapse is replayed from the embedded certificate by an exact finite checker; finite exhaustive verification is the proof mechanism for the 510 proper vertex subsets. No independent audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is specific to the standard nine-vertex triangulation. It proves existence of explicit elementary collapse sequences for all proper nonface-induced subcomplexes, but does not assert uniqueness of collapse order, shellability, or extension to other triangulations.
title: Every proper nonface in Kühnel's nine-vertex \(\mathbb{CP}^{2}\) collapses to a tetrahedral sphere
